claims.claim: Proof begins by trying to destroy the claim instead of defend it.
claims.plain_english: Instead of gathering evidence to support an idea, you first try to find every way it could be wrong. If it survives all those attacks, then it's proven.
claims.evidence_given: The document presents this as its core method and describes a four-move structure (Forward Method, Reverse Method, Kill Conditions, Survivor Identity) that implements this approach.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a claim could be proven true without ever being tested against its strongest objections, or if destroying alternatives never leads to a surviving claim.

claims.claim: The reader watches alternatives die instead of being asked to trust the ending.
claims.plain_english: The reader sees each possible explanation get ruled out one by one, so they don't have to just take the author's word for the final answer.
claims.evidence_given: This phrase is repeated three times in the document as the central description of the method's effect on the reader.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the reader could accept the conclusion without seeing alternatives eliminated, or if eliminating alternatives did not lead to a unique survivor.

claims.claim: The interlude sends the reader to the canonical page instead of replacing it.
claims.plain_english: This short version points you to the full, detailed version rather than trying to be the complete explanation itself.
claims.evidence_given: The document states: 'The interlude sends the reader to the canonical page instead of replacing it' and provides a link to the full treatment.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the interlude contained the full argument and made the canonical page redundant, or if the canonical page did not exist.

claims.claim: The page names the load-bearing structure before asking the reader to follow the full derivation.
claims.plain_english: First you see the main supporting points, then you go into the detailed reasoning. The overview comes before the deep dive.
claims.evidence_given: The document lists the four moves (Forward Method, Reverse Method, Kill Conditions, Survivor Identity) as the load-bearing structure, and then directs to the canonical page for the full derivation.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the reader needed the full derivation to understand the structure, or if the structure was not actually load-bearing.

claims.claim: Start with everything that could kill the idea, and let the survivor earn its name last.
claims.plain_english: Begin by listing all the ways the idea could be wrong. Only after it survives all those tests does it deserve to be called true.
claims.evidence_given: This is the subtitle of the document and is presented as the core instruction for the method.
claims.what_would_break_it: If an idea could be proven without considering its potential flaws, or if surviving all known objections did not guarantee truth.

claims.claim: The full canonical treatment remains linked below for the complete argument, tables, proofs, and source structure.
claims.plain_english: The detailed version with all the evidence, charts, and sources is available through a link. This page is just a summary.
claims.evidence_given: The document states this explicitly and provides a link to the canonical page.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the canonical page did not contain the complete argument, tables, proofs, and source structure as promised.
